Buyer’s own licensing; the seller’s nontransferable licence does not pass with equipment

sections.heading: A business licence does not supply the workforce
paragraphs: The U.S. Department of Labor describes a CW-1 route with employer conditions, prevailing-wage, recruitment and temporary labour-certification steps. A prevailing-wage determination is the programme’s wage decision for the actual job and worksite. Approved labour certification must come before the separate petition to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Certification alone does not authorise employment.

First test whether the plan can recruit and pay its local management team. If an overseas technician is essential, identify that person’s actual job and lawful route before promising a customer start date. CW-1 is not a promise of a place under a numerical limit or permission to move the worker to Guam or the mainland.

sections.heading: Check the other legal boundaries
paragraphs: The federal Franchise Rule includes franchises located in U.S. territories, subject to its exemptions. Independent territorial sales, dealer, relationship, advertising and sector requirements are not established as absent by this guide. They remain questions to investigate.

CNMI is outside the defined U.S. customs territory. Goods, quarantine and the receiving party need separate route-specific instructions. Do not use a mainland import spreadsheet as the legal answer for the islands.

sections.heading: What the management team should produce
paragraphs: Make a line-by-location licence list, with company records alongside it and renewal dates based on the issued licences. Add a staffing schedule showing employer, duties, worksite, wage evidence, recruitment, approvals and proposed start. Assign missing fees and dates to a person for investigation. These planning documents help prevent one uncompleted task from being hidden inside a confident opening date.

practicalOutput: A business-line/location licence list linked to a job-specific staffing and launch schedule.
limitations: This guide covers named issues only. It does not establish that an offer, sale, work assignment, import or opening is authorised. Local, sector and current transaction-specific questions remain to be reviewed.
learningSummary: A licence for one operation should not be treated as permission for every new site or service. The Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, often shortened to CNMI, has a business-licensing rule tied to business lines and locations. A partner’s company registration and a worker’s immigration permission are different records.

keyTerms.meaning: The Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, including islands such as Saipan and Tinian.
A distinct activity carried on by the business; the responsible authority must confirm how the proposed activities are classified.
The licence cannot simply be handed to a new owner with the equipment or assets.
The office dealing with company-registration documents, distinct from the Finance business-licence process.
A specific temporary-worker programme for qualifying CNMI employment; it is not general permission to work elsewhere in the United States.

seoTitle: CNMI business licences: activity, location and nontransferability

title: American Samoa: separate company permission, business licensing and people
description: Identify the trading entity, ownership-linked review and annual business-licence tasks; keep the visiting trainer’s approval on a separate track.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Begin with the entity that will trade
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s checklist describes a foreign-corporation permit application using certified company documents, corporate authorisation and resident-agent information. It separately directs the business to obtain business licensing before transacting business. The checklist identifies domestic and nonprofit corporations as exceptions to that named foreign-corporation law; the correct rules still depend on the actual entity type.

Write down which company will sign customers, employ the staff and receive the local revenue. An overseas brand owner and an independent operator are not automatically the same applicant. Then identify whether a parent company, local subsidiary or partner has the particular filing task.

sections.heading: Ownership can affect the review route
paragraphs: The official 2024 administrative compilation describes Territorial Planning Commission review linked to the applicant and ownership structure, and a separate immigration-board policy for business-licence applications submitted by people classified as aliens under the applicable rules. This guide does not decide any person’s American Samoan, residency or other legal status.

Prepare the ownership and control facts and ask the relevant agencies which route applies to this applicant. The compilation must be read with statutory definitions and any later changes. Avoid choosing an ownership label merely because it seems to make the form easier.

sections.heading: Worked example: a founder stays abroad but a trainer travels
paragraphs: Fictional example. An Asian facilities brand appoints a partner to run local contracts while its founder stays at home. The local partner says the brand agreement is signed, so it is ready to launch. The operations team discovers that an overseas supervisor must spend several weeks training crews at customer sites.

There are now several separate decisions. The company secretary identifies the operating entity’s permit and licence route. The local lead checks ownership-linked review. The people lead describes the supervisor’s actual tasks, dates and sponsor or employer. Calling the trip training does not establish permission to perform the work. The team keeps the customer launch date conditional while the necessary person-specific approval remains unresolved.

sections.heading: Try the decision: does the signed brand agreement complete the launch?
paragraphs: Use the fictional founder-abroad and visiting-trainer example. The local partner has signed the agreement. Ask which evidence belongs to the company, which belongs to ownership review, and which belongs to the individual who will train crews at customer sites.

Answer: the agreement establishes the agreed private rights, not completion of the public processes. The company file needs the actual trading entity and applicable foreign-corporation/business-licence route. The ownership file needs the facts relevant to the 2024 compilation’s described review, read with statutory definitions and later changes; this guide does not classify anyone’s legal status. The trainer file needs the person’s actual tasks, dates and employer or sponsor for the separate territorial enquiry.

Put business-licence renewal on the company calendar: the reviewed Commerce page identifies calendar-year expiry and October 1–December 31 renewal, with distinct late-fee and suspension treatment described above. Those dates cannot be copied into the trainer’s approval record. Use the companion people guide for that enquiry and retain the customer launch as conditional while a necessary answer is missing.

sections.heading: Entry approval is not a mainland visa assumption
paragraphs: American Samoa Legal Affairs explains that its entry rules differ from those of the United States and gives separate visitor and residency routes. Its residency instructions describe employment- and family-based petitions and say they must be approved before entry. A mainland U.S. visa, an ESTA travel assumption or a company business licence does not supply that territorial approval.
Record a non-sensitive summary of the person’s work, duration, employer or sponsor and approval status. Keep passports and actual immigration files in the authorised process outside this site.

Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa and the U.S. Virgin Islands are outside that defined area. Each therefore needs its own destination-and-route investigation.

This is a boundary finding, not a calculation. It supplies neither a duty rate nor permission for a product to enter. It also does not decide the treatment of a later shipment from a territory to the mainland. Those are additional questions about the actual goods and route.

sections.heading: Use the comparison to ask the right next question

title: CNMI CW-1 staffing: what must happen before a worker can start?

sections.heading: Keep the stages in the right relationship
paragraphs: The DOL page describes prevailing-wage, required U.S.-worker recruitment and temporary labour-certification steps. The employer needs approved temporary labour certification before the separate USCIS petition. Completing the labour application alone does not establish that the person may start work.

Ask for the current requirements and evidence at each stage, including the separate approval and status needed for employment. This guide does not choose an occupation code, predict availability under a numerical limit or decide anyone’s eligibility.

sections.heading: Worked example: a pilot needing a commissioning technician
paragraphs: Fictional example. A technical-services brand expects to hire a local manager but needs an overseas technician to put customer equipment into service. The sales team promises a fixed launch date because the specialist has agreed to travel.

Agreement to travel is not the missing legal evidence. The people lead first identifies the actual employer, job and worksite, then maps recruitment, wage and certification requirements and the separate immigration stage. Answer: those commercial or preparatory events do not supply work permission. The reviewed route connects employer/job facts, prevailing-wage and recruitment steps to approved temporary labour certification before the separate USCIS petition. Certification alone does not authorise employment. Keep the local manager’s hiring plan and the overseas technician’s route as separate records rather than treating “staffing ready” as one event.

title: American Samoa visiting trainers: check activities before arranging travel
description: Describe a trainer’s actual work, dates and sponsor before selecting the territorial entry or residence route; company licensing is a separate task.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The territorial instructions are the starting point
paragraphs: American Samoa Legal Affairs says that its entry rules differ from those of the United States and gives separate visitor and residency routes. Its residency page describes employment- and family-based petitions and says they must be completed and approved before entry. The applicable route still depends on the individual and the intended activities.

A mainland visa, a franchise agreement or the corporation’s business licence does not answer those person-specific questions. Keep the proposed visit, residence and physical work separate when describing the facts.

sections.heading: Worked example: four weeks described as training
paragraphs: Fictional example. A European facilities brand schedules four weeks of training in American Samoa. The visiting supervisor will show local staff procedures, direct crews during live contracts and resolve customer problems. The team assumes the trip is routine because it is short and the visitor remains employed overseas.

The people lead replaces the broad label with a daily activity description. It records the work locations, duration, local sponsor or employer, reporting line and customer-facing duties. Those facts allow the responsible process to be checked. This article does not classify the trip as permitted or prohibited; it shows why its name alone is insufficient. If approval is not supported, operations needs an alternative delivery plan rather than an unsupported promise that the trainer will arrive.

sections.heading: Try the decision: does “four weeks of training” answer the question?
paragraphs: Use the fictional trainer above, who will also direct live crews and troubleshoot customer work. Ask whether the short itinerary, overseas employment or the word training determines the applicable territorial route.

Answer: none of those descriptions alone supplies the permission. The people lead needs a non-sensitive account of the actual duties, dates, relevant status facts and employer or sponsor, then the applicable territorial instructions. American Samoa’s entry arrangements are distinct from mainland U.S. assumptions, and the reviewed residency instructions say the employment- and family-based petitions described there must be approved before entry.

The useful output is a specific unanswered question with a responsible person, not an invented visa category or a conclusion that the trainer may work. Keep the business’s annual licence renewal on a different calendar and private identity/immigration documents in the authorised process outside this site.

sections.heading: Write a useful brief without collecting private files
paragraphs: Record nationality and current status only as factual inputs to be checked through the authorised process. The actual passport, immigration application and sensitive supporting records belong in the authorised private process. The planning brief needs a reference and responsible person, not copies of those documents.

sections.heading: Keep the business’s annual calendar separate
paragraphs: Commerce’s business-licence page states calendar-year expiry and an October 1–December 31 renewal period, with separately described late-fee and suspension treatment. The operating entity needs that calendar even when a visiting worker’s timing changes.

A renewed business licence is evidence about the business’s licensing process, not proof of the supervisor’s immigration status. Conversely, a person’s approval does not renew the company’s licence. Put the two records on separate lines and identify who maintains each.

sections.heading: What to decide before booking
paragraphs: Confirm which route is being investigated, what approval must precede entry and what evidence will support the proposed work. Link any unresolved person-specific step to the training or customer-start date. If the essential person cannot start in time, decide whether another supported staffing arrangement, a different service scope or a later launch is workable.

title: Pittsburgh business registration: outside offices and city customer work
description: Check the actual city service and commencement facts, the published 15-day provision and Finance verification before calling registration complete.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Why the customer location matters
paragraphs: The city’s official registration page includes a business located outside Pittsburgh that performs work or services in whole or in part within the city. The operating lead therefore needs the actual customer sites and activities, not only the company’s registered office.

The page quotes a 15-day registration provision. Match that provision to the actual commencement facts before fixing the business’s due date. A missing start date should prompt a question, not a guessed date or an assumption that no registration is needed.

sections.heading: The form and the confirmation are different records
paragraphs: The same page says registration is not complete until Finance issues verification. Keep the submitted information and the issued confirmation separately so the team can see which stage has been reached. A payment receipt or account reference may help track an application, but it should not be relabelled as the verification itself.

This distinction matters when another team relies on the registration before making a commitment. The useful question is “What record confirms this stage is complete?” rather than “Has someone started the paperwork?”

sections.heading: Worked example: crews crossing the city boundary
paragraphs: Fictional example. A foreign cleaning brand’s partner rents an office outside Pittsburgh. It wins a contract to clean a customer’s premises inside the city and assumes its office municipality is the only place to investigate.

The COO records the local contracting entity, customer address, service and actual start date. Finance checks the city provision against those facts and follows the registration process if applicable. It then retains the verification when issued. If the application has only been submitted, the plan says so; it does not display “registered” merely because a form or payment was sent.

sections.heading: Try the decision: submitted or registered?
paragraphs: In the fictional cleaning example, the partner’s office is outside Pittsburgh and its customer’s premises are inside. Before reading the answer, identify the relevant activity and commencement facts, then decide what an application confirmation would prove.

Answer: the official page includes an outside business performing work or services wholly or partly in Pittsburgh, so the customer-site work belongs in the enquiry. Match the quoted 15-day provision to the actual commencement facts rather than inventing a deadline from the contract-signing or incorporation date. This exercise supplies no date calculation because those actual facts must first be established.

An application confirmation proves submission. The page says registration is not complete until Finance issues verification, so the team should keep a separate field for that issued record. Any premises, regulated-work or franchise-sales question remains separate even after the registration stage is complete.

sections.heading: What this registration does not decide
paragraphs: A registration record is different from permission to use a particular premises or carry on regulated professional work. If the business also opens a depot or performs a regulated activity, the premises or technical lead must investigate that separate question. The city registration also does not determine whether the overseas brand’s commercial arrangement is a franchise or whether its sales process meets disclosure rules.
Keep uncertain fees and additional requirements visible. This guide explains one published process; it is not evidence that every other obligation has been checked.

sections.heading: Make a city-work register
paragraphs: List the operating entity, each relevant Pittsburgh site, the service, commencement facts and person responsible for the registration decision. Attach references to the application and issued verification, then identify any separate premises or sector questions. This is a practical management record, not an additional filing created by this guide.

practicalOutput: A record of the actual city work, its timing and the application/verification evidence.

learningSummary: A service partner may keep its office in a neighbouring municipality and send crews into Pittsburgh. The relevant question is not simply where the office is registered. The city’s published process can cover work or services performed wholly or partly inside the city.

title: Atlanta: separate the occupation-tax certificate from zoning review
description: Distinguish ATLBIZ tax certification from Accela zoning and applicable permits; payment or submission does not prove an issued opening record.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Two applications can support one opening
paragraphs: The current ATL311 instruction separates the occupation-tax application in ATLBIZ from a location zoning review through Accela. It also identifies applicable regulatory permits. These steps answer different questions: identifying the business for the tax process does not establish that the location is suitable for its proposed use.

Use the legal entity, actual activity and address consistently. A general description such as “services” may hide storage, equipment or customer visits that the premises team needs to describe. Ask which reviews apply to the real proposal rather than treating the agency’s whole directory as a universal permit list.

sections.heading: Issuance comes after the required material
paragraphs: The instructions describe issuance following required documents and payment. An account, submitted application or application charge is therefore not the certificate. Record what has been submitted, what other review is outstanding and what issued document will show completion.

A processing estimate can help organise the schedule, but it is not a guaranteed opening date. The business should link any customer or premises commitment to the actual approvals that commitment depends on.

sections.heading: Worked example: the portal looks complete
paragraphs: Fictional example. A partner sets up ATLBIZ and pays an application charge. Its manager tells the overseas brand that Atlanta licensing is finished. The proposed unit’s zoning approval has not yet been obtained.

The launch lead asks for the issued certificate and discovers the missing location task. The premises lead takes responsibility for the zoning review and the evidence needed in the application process. The team records the tax application as submitted and the overall certificate as pending. It does not assume paying again or opening another account would resolve the zoning question.

sections.heading: Try the decision: why is the paid application still incomplete?
paragraphs: Use the fictional portal example above. Finance can show a payment and a submitted tax application, but zoning review is unfinished. Ask which document establishes the tax-application stage and which evidence is missing for the proposed site.

Answer: Atlanta’s occupation-tax process and the location review are different tasks, using the ATLBIZ and Accela processes described above. Required documents and payment precede issuance; a payment is not the issued certificate. Unfinished zoning cannot be marked complete merely because a related tax screen looks complete.

The project lead should return separate evidence for the tax application/certificate, zoning outcome and any activity-specific permit that actually applies. That is not a universal list or fixed sequence for every Atlanta business, and no submitted date is a guaranteed opening or processing date.

sections.heading: Organise the documents by the question they answer
paragraphs: Keep entity and trading-name information together, location/use evidence together, and the occupation-tax application, payment and issued certificate together. Add a separate row for any activity-specific permit. This lets the business see whether the problem is identity, premises, missing documents, payment or a separate regulated activity.
Other tax, employment, sector and franchise-sales questions remain independent. This guide’s narrow city process does not classify the brand agreement or supply all permissions for the work.

sections.heading: A useful next request

practicalOutput: A linked application checklist showing the tax, zoning and applicable permit stages separately.
limitations: This guide covers named issues only. It does not establish that an offer, sale, work assignment, import or opening is authorised. Local, sector and current transaction-specific questions remain to be reviewed.

title: City of Miami: check the use certificate and city/county tax receipts

sections.heading: Find the correct local government first
paragraphs: Record the exact premises and whether they are inside City of Miami boundaries. The customer’s mailing label or a commercial description of the area does not settle that question. Once the authority is known, use its process for the actual activity. A county instruction for an unincorporated area should not simply be copied onto a City of Miami unit.

sections.heading: The city generally puts use before the tax receipt
paragraphs: The city’s published process generally sequences a Certificate of Use before its Business Tax Receipt, while stating exceptions. Check whether the use requirement or an exception fits the actual proposal; do not assume every business follows an identical route.

The city also directs businesses to a separate Miami-Dade County local business tax receipt. Keep city and county records distinct. Obtaining one does not demonstrate that the other was obtained or that a premises review has been completed.

sections.heading: Worked example: a depot serving customers across the county
paragraphs: Fictional example. A service operator stores equipment in a City of Miami unit and sends teams to customers throughout Miami-Dade. The manager receives county guidance and assumes it describes every approval for the depot.

The wider customer service area is also recorded for any additional questions, but it does not change the depot’s municipality. If an exception is claimed, the file records its actual basis instead of leaving the use-certificate box blank.

sections.heading: Try the decision: which Miami authority and which record?
paragraphs: Use the fictional depot serving county-wide customers. The actual depot is inside the City of Miami, but the manager has relied on a county guide. Ask whether its service territory or postal market label selects the local premises process.

Answer: start with the exact address and responsible local government. The City of Miami generally places its Certificate of Use before the city Business Tax Receipt, with stated exceptions; the Miami-Dade County receipt is separate. A site in unincorporated county territory calls for its own applicable route rather than automatic use of the city process.

For the city depot, record three distinct questions: the use certificate or applicable exception, the city receipt and the county receipt. Retain each actual issued record or supported exception. This is not a finding that those records complete fire, health, professional or every other opening requirement.

sections.heading: Keep site, tax and professional evidence separate
paragraphs: A use certificate, local tax receipt and professional credential serve different purposes. Describe the services accurately so any separate trade, health, fire or other activity question can be assigned to the appropriate person. This article does not supply those answers for an unidentified activity.

The same separation applies to the brand relationship. Government operating documents do not prove compliance with franchise-sales rules, and a private brand licence does not replace government records. Unknown fees or additional requirements remain questions to investigate.

sections.heading: The document to request from your local lead

For each, record applicability, current application or issued document, responsible person and next action. Then add any separately identified activity permissions. practicalOutput: An address-specific checklist distinguishing the city use decision, city tax receipt and county tax receipt.

title: Jacksonville: distinguish the business-tax receipt and occupancy decision
description: Keep the Local Business Tax Receipt, commercial occupancy question and any separate municipal route distinct for the actual address and proposed activity.

sections.heading: Two questions can remain open at different times
paragraphs: The local tax receipt concerns covered business activity. The Certificate of Use concerns the new or expanding commercial operation’s use process. The city’s tax page separates them, so recording one should not automatically close the other.

sections.heading: Check the municipality, not just the market name
paragraphs: The official instructions also identify additional municipal tax routes for the beach municipalities and Baldwin. sections.heading: Worked example: finance has a receipt, operations has a gap
paragraphs: Fictional example. A new commercial depot receives its local tax receipt. Finance marks that document as received and tells the overseas brand that the opening paperwork is finished. The use certificate is still unresolved.

The receipt is genuine evidence, but it answers only its own question. The launch lead keeps the premises-use task open and asks the premises lead for the required determination and document. A proposed second operation in Jacksonville Beach is put on a separate line for that municipality’s local-tax question. The team now has two clear outstanding decisions rather than one misleading green opening indicator.

sections.heading: Try the decision: can finance release both sites?
paragraphs: Use the fictional depot and Jacksonville Beach site above. Finance has a local tax receipt, but the depot’s occupancy question is unresolved. Ask whether that receipt also answers the new or expanding commercial-space enquiry or the second municipality’s route.

Answer: it answers only the process to which the receipt belongs. The Local Business Tax Receipt and the Certificate of Occupancy question are different, and the reviewed guidance identifies a separate occupancy enquiry for new or expanding commercial premises. The actual municipality also matters: the beaches municipalities and Baldwin have additional routes to investigate.

Keep one address row for the depot and another for the Jacksonville Beach proposal. In each, record the tax receipt, the actual use/occupancy question, applicable authority and missing evidence. Do not impose one universal sequence or label an unanswered second-site enquiry “not required.”

sections.heading: What to retain and who should answer
paragraphs: Keep the entity, actual activities, addresses and proposed start dates with the relevant applications and issued documents. Finance owns the tax-record evidence. The premises lead owns the use enquiry. A technical lead checks any separate regulated service. Their tasks may depend on one another, but one person’s completed record does not prove the whole operation is authorised.

sections.heading: A narrow process, not a complete permission list
paragraphs: Ask the local lead for a table showing the tax receipt, use certificate and applicable additional municipal questions, with an owner and evidence for each. Fees, sector requirements and unrelated obligations remain unknown where not checked. Neither a tax receipt nor a use record determines whether the brand’s agreement is a franchise or satisfies its sales-disclosure duties.

practicalOutput: A location-specific table distinguishing tax receipts, use evidence and additional municipal questions.
limitations: This guide covers named issues only. It does not establish that an offer, sale, work assignment, import or opening is authorised. Local, sector and current transaction-specific questions remain to be reviewed.
learningSummary: A local operator may receive a business-tax receipt while another opening task remains unfinished. Jacksonville’s instructions expressly distinguish that receipt from the Certificate of Use for a new or expanding commercial business. The actual address matters too, particularly for beach municipalities and Baldwin.

title: Kansas City, Missouri: separate zoning, city licensing and trade work

reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Confirm which city is responsible
paragraphs: Start with the actual premises and municipality. A commercial sales territory does not identify the government office responsible for the site. An address in Kansas requires a different jurisdictional investigation from an address covered by this Missouri guide.

Also identify the operating entity and describe what happens at the site: office administration, storage, workshop activity, customer visits or actual trade work. These facts make the enquiry usable for the authority rather than leaving it at the broad label “industrial services.”

sections.heading: What the BizCare guide separates
paragraphs: The official guide identifies zoning clearance for new businesses with a KCMO address and address changes, city registration or licensing, and additional industry requirements. A location decision, a business record and a permission for regulated work answer different questions.

The general guidance acknowledges state-law exemptions. Check whether an actual exemption fits the activity instead of treating it as permission for all businesses. Resolve the applicable prerequisites before licence issuance and operation; a completed online account is not a substitute for that evidence.

sections.heading: Worked example: the workshop and the construction task
paragraphs: Fictional example. An industrial-services partner rents a workshop at a KCMO address and intends to perform a regulated construction trade. It initially asks only for the city business licence.

The premises lead investigates whether the proposed workshop use has the necessary zoning clearance. Finance or the local operating lead handles the city business record. The technical lead separately checks the permission for the construction work. A licence in one column is not evidence in the others. If the business later moves, the published address-change point prompts another location enquiry rather than simply editing its stationery.

sections.heading: Try the decision: does “service company” describe enough?
paragraphs: Use the fictional industrial-services workshop above. Compare an office-only description with the actual storage, workshop activity and construction-related task. Ask which facts the BizCare/location enquiry needs and which belong to a trade-permission enquiry.

Answer: the broad service-company name is insufficient. For the Kansas City, Missouri site, describe the address, storage, equipment, customer access and actual work so the relevant location/zoning and city-licence routes can be identified. Keep the stated state-law exemptions in that licensing branch; this guide does not say every service has one identical city-licence duty.

A regulated construction or professional task needs its own actual-task enquiry, not permission inferred from the workshop’s city record. The exercise selects facts to investigate, not a final trade classification. It concerns Kansas City, Missouri, and supplies no process for Kansas City, Kansas.

sections.heading: Make the question specific enough to answer
paragraphs: Give the authority a written description of the entity, premises and services. Ask which city category and any state-law exemption are being considered, what evidence is needed for the address and which office handles the regulated trade. Retain the answer with the relevant application or issued record.

Unknown fees remain unknown. The article does not supply every trade licence, tax or employment rule, or establish that an offer of franchise rights is permitted. Those questions stay separate from the narrow city opening process.

sections.heading: The useful management output
paragraphs: Prepare a three-part checklist: location clearance, city business record and activity-specific permission. Name an owner and the required evidence for each. This checklist is an optional way to coordinate the work; it should reveal missing answers rather than turn broad guidance into a claim that the premises can open.

practicalOutput: A KCMO address-and-activity checklist separating zoning, city licensing and regulated work.
limitations: This guide covers named issues only. It does not establish that an offer, sale, work assignment, import or opening is authorised. Local, sector and current transaction-specific questions remain to be reviewed.
learningSummary: A partner may describe its territory as Kansas City while planning work on different sides of a state boundary. This guide concerns Kansas City, Missouri, often abbreviated KCMO. Its city business guidance separates location zoning, city registration or licensing and industry-specific requirements.

title: Baltimore City: distinguish the licence clerk, County and tax account

sections.heading: The state and the clerk answer different questions
paragraphs: Maryland’s Comptroller separates sales/use-tax registration from business-licence categories that may apply through the Clerk of Circuit Court. Those licences are issued in the county or Baltimore City where the business is located. The actual activity determines which category needs investigation; this guide does not say every service business needs every clerk licence.

A state tax account identifies a tax-registration step. It does not prove that the operator has obtained an applicable licence, that the premises have approved use or that a worker holds a professional qualification.

sections.heading: Why the address changes the enquiry
paragraphs: A contact sheet headed Baltimore County is not automatically appropriate for a Baltimore City premises. Confirm the legal jurisdiction from the actual address before choosing the clerk. Keep the proposed operating entity and trading name with that address so the records refer to the same business.

This matters when a brand serves the wider Baltimore market from several locations. Market coverage is a commercial description; the licence application still needs the relevant government area and activity.

sections.heading: Worked example: adding equipment sales to a service workshop
paragraphs: Fictional example. A service operator adds a workshop selling equipment in Baltimore City. Its accountant starts with a Baltimore County contact list and points to the existing sales-tax account as evidence that registration is finished.

The company secretary corrects the jurisdiction and describes the actual mix of goods and services to the City clerk’s process. The team asks which category applies and retains the resulting instructions or issued licence. Finance keeps the state tax account as separate evidence. The enquiry does not assume equipment sales and servicing receive identical treatment, or that the address can be ignored because the brand already operates elsewhere.

sections.heading: Try the decision: which office answers the added-sales question?
paragraphs: Use the fictional workshop that adds equipment sales. The accountant has a Maryland tax account and Baltimore County contact details. Ask whether those records establish the City licence category for the actual activity.

Answer: neither settles that category. Baltimore City is distinct from Baltimore County. The state Comptroller’s sales/use-tax account and the Clerk of the Circuit Court’s business-licensing role answer different questions. Here the clerk is being consulted about an administrative licensing process, not because the business has a lawsuit.

Prepare the City address, legal operator and separate service/sales activities for the correct enquiry. Whether a particular licence category applies depends on the activity; the exercise does not declare every service subject to the same licence or decide the workshop’s final category.

sections.heading: Prepare the records in a way another person can check
paragraphs: Create one row for the state tax account, one for the clerk category decision and any required issued licence, and one for premises or regulated-work questions identified separately. Include the exact entity, address, activity, authority and responsible person. Distinguish an application or payment from the actual issued record.

Use the current instructions for fees and timing. Nothing here establishes all local, trade, employment or franchise-sales requirements. If the category is uncertain, record the question and the person obtaining the answer rather than entering “not required” without support.

practicalOutput: A City-versus-County jurisdiction check and a separate state-tax/clerk-licence evidence list.
limitations: This guide covers named issues only. It does not establish that an offer, sale, work assignment, import or opening is authorised. Local, sector and current transaction-specific questions remain to be reviewed.
learningSummary: A Baltimore-area business can have the right state tax account and still need to investigate a separate business-licence category. It also needs the correct local office: Baltimore City and Baltimore County are different jurisdictions. Begin with the address and the goods or services actually provided.

title: A Brunei service business: test the American customer before selling territory
description: Use BEDB introductions to prepare one U.S. service-contract test, separating customer evidence, goods paperwork and actual decision authority.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Ask Brunei’s support agency a question it can help answer
paragraphs: A service company may already know how to run branches at home but still need to learn how American customers buy. The Brunei Economic Development Board describes export-readiness help, preliminary market information and business matching. Ask whether its assistance fits your particular service and proposed delivery arrangement. Its showcase of products does not establish demand for a facilities or technical-service business.

Start with a customer problem: for example, what evidence would a property manager need before allowing your team into a building? That is more useful than asking for an American partner without explaining whether you want a customer, supplier or independent business operator.

sections.heading: Goods need a different file from the brand and training
paragraphs: Brunei’s customs registration or agent process concerns companies moving goods. Permission to use a brand, training delivered online and a shipment of cleaning chemicals are different activities. If the service depends on a particular supply, name the exporter, the U.S. importer and the person who can approve a substitute.

The exact controls for an actual product have not been researched here. Brunei export paperwork would not, by itself, settle U.S. import requirements or whether the operator may use that product at a customer’s site.

sections.heading: Three records answer three different questions
paragraphs: A useful introduction, a goods-registration record and a service pilot can all belong in the expansion file. They do not prove the same thing. The comparison below uses the existing preparation choices; it creates no additional BEDB condition.

A contact or information relevant to the proposed customer problem

sections.heading: Fictional example: an introduction exposes a pricing problem
paragraphs: A Brunei facilities-service group meets an American property manager through a support programme. Its owner wants to offer rights across a state. The operations manager notices that every overseas quotation still requires the owner’s approval, so the introduction has not yet proved that the business can work through an independent operator.

The team chooses one customer specification for a limited pilot. It records who may approve the price, cover absent staff, handle a complaint and collect the invoice. It then compares shipping the proprietary chemical with a separately priced U.S. substitute, including any effect on service quality. These are recommended planning tests, not conditions imposed by the support agency. A sensible result may be to change the method or delay wider rights.

sections.heading: Do not turn a country listing into permission to work
paragraphs: The reviewed U.S. State Department table lists Brunei for E-1, not E-2. Those categories are different. The listing helps identify a question to investigate; it does not approve an owner, employee or investment. If someone will work physically in America, record nationality, ownership and control, proposed activities and actual role. The owner can remain abroad while the commercial plan is prepared.

sections.heading: Prepare a short pilot brief
bullets: Expansion lead: describe the service and target customer, then ask the Board two specific support questions.
Operations lead: name who can price, deliver and remedy one contract without the owner.
Supply lead: list physical goods, specifications, exporter/importer roles and unresolved product controls.
Finance lead: separate goods sales, service fees, royalties, support costs and expected collection dates; obtain the actual payment and tax analysis.
Pilot lead: set a date to review the evidence and decide whether to stop, change or expand the test.

practicalOutput: A support enquiry and one-contract pilot brief that separates service delivery, physical supplies, payments and proposed U.S. work.
limitations: This is a scoped origin decision guide, not complete origin or U.S. legal coverage. Home-country tax, banking, sector permissions, privacy/IP and U.S. location obligations still need fact-specific review. No professional legal review has been performed.
learningSummary: An introduction to an American buyer can help a Brunei business start a conversation, but it does not show that an American manager can deliver the service profitably. This guide explains how to use Brunei’s support and goods-export routes while keeping American operating and immigration questions separate.

sections.heading: Separate the three things the American operator would receive
paragraphs: Before quoting, list the rights to use the brand or manuals, the training and continuing support, and every physical item. This makes it possible to identify who owes each part of the service and which authority may be relevant. A customs development in Cambodia does not classify the American operating relationship or authorise the product’s use in the United States.

Cambodia’s official September 2026 report describes a new electronic Certificate of Origin system. It matters when goods move. It does not mean that a foreign operator has permission to trade under your brand or that all supplies will enter America at a preferred duty rate.

sections.heading: Understand the announcement’s limited finding
paragraphs: The announcement identifies co.moc.gov.kh for electronic certificates under preferential and non-preferential arrangements. It also refers to implementing Prakas and a free-trade-agreement information portal. This review read the announcement, not the complete implementing instruments or a product-specific claim to preference.

For the actual goods, obtain the current procedure and supporting supplier records. Do not use a certificate application as a universal tariff exemption or treat a convenient description of the kit as proof of every component’s origin.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a training company ships a maintenance kit
paragraphs: A Cambodian training and technical-services business plans to license its method to an American operator. Its kit contains components made by several suppliers. The operating manager sees that packing the box in Phnom Penh does not, by itself, establish that every component has Cambodian origin.

She creates a bill of materials with a supplier and origin record for each item. The U.S. importer and customs advisers can then assess the actual origin and tariff treatment. At the same time, the technical lead tests whether a locally available substitute could deliver the same service. If substitution changes safety, performance or the promised standard, that change goes into the method and budget. These are planning choices; the guide does not invent a new approval process for substitutes.

sections.heading: A completed goods-and-rights comparison for the kit

sections.heading: Build the transaction description before drawing a conclusion
paragraphs: The Burma regulations address specified property interests and dealings involving blocked persons. Other directives and sanctions programmes may also matter. Identify the actual contracting company, owners, banks, activity and connection to the United States before promising that a payment can be made.

This guide does not screen a particular person or find that a company is blocked. It explains what information the responsible sanctions adviser needs. U.S. restrictions, non-U.S. obligations and a bank’s own commercial policy are separate questions, even when each can stop the same payment.

sections.heading: A clear name search does not settle ownership
paragraphs: OFAC explains that an entity can be blocked when one or more blocked persons own, in aggregate, 50% or more of it, directly or indirectly. An unlisted company name is therefore not enough: the ownership chain matters. Control and other designation or directive issues also require their own attention.

A bank declining a transfer does not provide a complete legal analysis either. It may be applying a risk policy that differs from the legal restriction. Record what the bank decided and its stated reason without turning it into a general statement about every transaction.

sections.heading: Follow ownership and the payment as separate paths

The finance manager asks who owns that distributor, who ultimately benefits from the money and which activity the payment supports. The new account name has not removed the original questions.

She maps each account, intermediary, currency and intended recipient. The technical director identifies the equipment, end users and support to be supplied. If ownership or authorisation is unresolved, they obtain the missing evidence or pause the proposal. They do not route money around an alert. A previous successful transfer, introduction or completed checklist would not establish that this transaction is permitted.

sections.heading: Follow the client contract into the operating company
paragraphs: Identify who signs the client contract, employs and directs personnel, invoices the account and handles an incident outside office hours. Those responsibilities must be workable even if the brand owner stays overseas.

This guide examines California PPO licensing. Alarm services, investigations, armed work and other states require their own category analysis. Do not use the breadth of the word security to assume one licence covers everything.

sections.heading: A new entity needs its own licensing analysis
paragraphs: The October 2025 BSIS application packet says each entity needs its own PPO application, that licences cannot be transferred or assigned to new entities, and that each company licence designates a qualified manager in active charge. The Bureau must also authorise the business name. Approval of a company name by the Secretary of State is a different decision and is not automatic BSIS approval. Keep the name, applicant entity and qualified-manager evidence aligned before promising a client start.

Personnel registration, training and weapon-specific permissions are separate layers to verify before assignments. Company approval alone does not settle them. Branch requirements and actual exemptions also remain specific questions.

It requires occurrence cover and does not accept claims-made cover for this requirement. Those are operating conditions, not a quotation of the premium.

A client may separately request a higher limit, additional-insured status, indemnity or cyber coverage. Identify whether a requirement comes from the regulator or the customer, obtain an actual quote and review the contract’s risks. Meeting the stated minimum does not establish insurance sufficiency for every account.

sections.heading: Follow the work and the contracts
paragraphs: California’s Labor Commissioner administers the registration program described here. Its janitorial-employer explanation includes a person or entity employing a covered worker or engaging through contracts, subcontracts or franchise arrangements for covered janitorial services. The covered worker may be an employee, independent contractor or franchisee predominantly working as a janitor.

The agency’s frequently asked questions expressly include a commercial cleaning provider without employees and a provider using franchisees or contractors. Calling every operator an independent business therefore does not establish that the provider is outside this particular program.

sections.heading: A customer’s exception does not automatically protect the provider
paragraphs: The agency distinguishes the business receiving cleaning from the business supplying it. Its example is a restaurant hiring a cleaner after closing: the restaurant is acting as the recipient. That is a different role from a brand company arranging commercial cleaning for customers.

The FAQ also excludes a provider that only cleans residential dwellings and gives the agency’s interpretation for public entities; the reviewed rule describes the program as applying to private entities. Apply those examples to the actual role and work. They do not create a general exception for every intermediary between the customer and cleaner.

sections.heading: Register and renew for the actual legal entity
paragraphs: The current program states a $500 nonrefundable initial application fee and a $500 annual renewal fee. Registration lasts one year. Renewal is due by the month and day on which the original registration was issued, so record the issued registration rather than simply adding a year to the date someone started filling in the form.

Section 13810 asks for entity details and information about customers and contractors or franchisees. Workers’ compensation evidence is conditional on the applicant employing one or more employees. Do not extend that condition to every covered worker: this program’s worker definition can also include contractors and franchisees.

sections.heading: Keep registration and worker records useful after filing
paragraphs: Assign the required three-year employee and other covered-worker records, including work periods and compensation. A registration number alone does not provide those records. The application and renewal owner should also retain the legal names, business names, ownership information and relevant entity documents.

When entering, extending, renewing or modifying a janitorial contract, review the counterparty’s registration as the cited requirements direct. Keep the registration details, expiry and contract date together. This is a practical way to see which provider was checked for which agreement.

title: California janitorial sexual-violence and harassment-prevention training
description: Covered janitorial workers and supervisors have specific training times, providers, content and records.

sections.heading: Identify the people before booking a course
paragraphs: The program covers nonsupervisory covered workers and their supervisors. Because covered workers can include contractors and franchisees predominantly doing janitorial work, the list should follow the actual people and roles, not just the employee payroll. A franchise agreement does not prove that every cleaner or supervisor has received compliant training.

Name the janitorial employer responsible for each group. This matters where a brand, local franchisee, subcontractor and training organization all participate: someone still needs to know whose legal duty is being fulfilled.

sections.heading: Give new roles and recurring training separate dates
paragraphs: Section 13821 requires at least two hours of training at least once every two years, and training within six months after assuming a new covered position. If the training is split into segments, each segment must last at least one hour. Record the position-start date as well as the course date; a calendar based only on the company’s annual registration renewal can miss the new-position deadline.

A defined successor employer may use a retained worker’s documented last-training date only when the rule’s workforce-retention, seniority, wage and policy conditions are satisfied. Taking over a customer contract alone does not establish all those conditions. Preserve the previous training record and check the full successor requirements before carrying the date forward.

sections.heading: Check the provider, content and language
paragraphs: California’s Department of Industrial Relations, or DIR, says in-person compliance must begin following publication of the qualified-organization list in January 2024. The program distinguishes qualified peer trainers for nonsupervisory workers from qualified supervisor trainers. Select the route for the participants actually being trained.

The required content is developed through the Labor Occupational Health Program, known as LOHP, under DIR’s direction. Training must match the language and literacy understood by the participants. A general online orientation or an English-only certificate does not, by itself, prove that the required provider, content, format and understanding requirements were met.

sections.heading: The employer keeps the records
paragraphs: The regulation places the proof responsibility on the employer even when another entity or janitorial employer provides training. Keep the required records for at least three years and make them available to the Labor Commissioner. Outsourcing the lesson does not outsource the need to demonstrate compliance.

title: California pay planning: check the hourly rate, then test the manager’s role
description: The general 2026 minimum wage and an executive salary calculation are starting points, not automatic answers for every worksite or manager.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Price the work at its real location
paragraphs: California’s MW-2026 order sets the general minimum at $16.90 per hour from January 1, 2026, subject to its application provisions. The order identifies separate fast-food and healthcare requirements, and the Department of Industrial Relations explains that local requirements may be higher.

For a business serving several customer sites, check every actual worksite and industry. A headquarters address or a metropolitan-area label does not establish the rate for all places where staff work. The hourly minimum is also not an all-in employment cost; finance must budget the other relevant costs separately.

sections.heading: A management title does not replace the duties test
paragraphs: The Labor Commissioner’s enforcement guidance describes conditions that must be considered together for the executive exemption. They include management of the enterprise or a recognized unit, regular direction of two or more employees, hiring or firing authority or recommendations given particular weight, discretion and independent judgment, primarily exempt duties, and the required salary.

Compare the planned job with the work actually performed. A launch manager who spends substantial time cleaning, delivering services or following a prescribed manual may raise different questions from a manager genuinely directing a unit. A salary increase alone does not resolve that duties analysis.

sections.heading: Keep the salary calculation separate from the wider budget
paragraphs: The executive entry describes a monthly salary of at least twice the state minimum for full-time employment and identifies a 40-hour full-time week. Using the 2026 general minimum produces an annualized planning equivalent of $70,304: $16.90 × 40 × 52 × 2.

This arithmetic illustrates the salary component. It does not find that any worker is exempt or that every industry uses this exact test. Employer taxes, benefits, insurance, recruitment and equipment are not automatically part of the guaranteed salary counted for the exemption. Keep the salary offer, duties assessment and total employer budget as three separate records.

sections.heading: Self-check: what does the $120,000 budget prove?
paragraphs: These are answers about the stated facts, not a classification of an actual worker or another exemption.

No. The actual duties and applicable wage order still need review.

This guide supplies no 2027 rate.

Although the total budget exceeds $70,304, the base salary does not meet the illustrated salary component. Finance cannot count every budget line as salary.

Suppose the business raises the guaranteed salary. That change fixes neither an unknown worksite rate nor an unexamined duties test. The team must still establish the relevant wage order and actual role, then model the correct pay basis and any applicable overtime. That can change what the customer contract needs to earn.

title: Texas employee vs independent contractor: evidence for unemployment tax
description: Use the Texas unemployment-tax inquiry before assuming a contract or a 1099 determines worker status.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Name the question being answered
paragraphs: TWC’s guidance concerns the Texas Unemployment Compensation Act. It identifies service, wages and direction or control, and explains that the right to control can be enough even if not exercised. An agreement, trading name or IRS form does not determine the result.

That is why the reviewer needs both the written contract and actual operations. A contract may reserve powers management rarely uses; a short agreement may also fail to describe the detailed instructions given every day. Neither document labels nor assumptions about tax reporting can replace the factual inquiry.

sections.heading: Use the twenty factors as evidence questions
paragraphs: TWC’s comparative guide examines instructions, training, integration into the business, personal service, helpers, continuing relationships, set hours, full-time requirements, work location, sequence, reports, payment, expenses, tools, investment, profit or loss, multiple clients, public availability, discharge and quitting.

Not every factor applies, and its weight can change with the business and facts. This is not a points contest in which eleven favourable answers guarantee a result. Explain what the relevant evidence shows and why, including disputed or mixed facts.

sections.heading: Compare a reserved power with what actually happens
paragraphs: The example raises questions rather than deciding status. A useful memo records both columns, explains mixed facts and identifies which actual document supports each answer.

headers: Actual practice and evidence to examine
rows: Who chooses the method and sequence?
Does the company reserve the power to dictate how the service is performed, even when it rarely intervenes?
The fictional company fixes the route and cleaning sequence. Retain the actual instructions, schedules and communications, not just the contractor label.
Who controls training, tools and help?
Who may require training, choose equipment, hire a helper or allow a substitute?
The fictional company supplies equipment and requires training. Compare that practice with contract clauses and records of who can make those decisions.
Who bears financial risk and serves other customers?
What do payment, expense, investment and termination terms actually allow?
The fictional weekly payment is one fact. Collect invoices, expenses, other-client and public-availability evidence before assessing independence.
Does issuing a 1099 answer the test?
A reporting label does not remove a retained right to control.
No. TWC weighs relevant factors in the Texas unemployment-tax context; there is no eleven-out-of-twenty pass mark and no automatic result for federal tax or wage law.

sections.heading: Worked example: a tightly directed cleaning route
paragraphs: Fictional example: a facilities company describes a worker as a contractor. The company fixes the service route, dictates the cleaning sequence, supplies equipment, requires its training and pays a fixed weekly amount. It plans to issue a 1099 and initially treats that as the end of the question.

The onboarding manager instead collects the contract, route instructions, training records, schedules and payment terms. The reviewer compares retained control rights with actual performance. Who can change the method, hire a helper or substitute someone? Who pays expenses, owns tools and bears the risk of an unprofitable job? Is the worker genuinely available to other customers?

Those facts raise the control issues TWC identifies; the example does not make a final classification. The company records a reasoned Texas unemployment-tax assessment or obtains TWC assistance before relying on the proposed arrangement. Issuing the form cannot cure an unsupported classification.

sections.heading: Turn the assessment into a working record
paragraphs: A useful memo links each relevant fact to an actual source: an invoice, manual, schedule, communication or contract clause. It should explain apparent contradictions instead of selecting only facts that favour the desired classification.

Assign a responsible person to review changes when the worker gains or loses genuine control or financial independence. The review belongs before payroll or contractor onboarding, with later changes documented. A conclusion for this role at this time should not be copied automatically to another state or another type of legal test.

sections.heading: Prepare the role-specific evidence checklist
bullets: Identify the worker, hiring entity, actual role and Texas unemployment-tax question.
Record who controls methods, sequence, hours, attendance and training.
List tools, expenses, helpers/substitutes, investment and potential profit or loss.
Check other clients, public availability, repeated engagements and termination rights.
Attach operational examples and a reasoned assessment; leave federal wage and tax tests separately assigned.

practicalOutput: A Texas unemployment-tax classification memo linking relevant control and independence facts to actual documents and identifying separate legal tests.
limitations: This is the stated Texas unemployment-tax inquiry, not a complete employment, franchise, licensing, federal-tax or local-law review.
Actual entity, worker, worksite, industry and date facts matter. No classification, exemption or arrangement is approved; the result must not be copied across legal regimes without review.
learningSummary: A company may call someone an independent contractor while keeping detailed control over the job. For Texas unemployment tax, the actual working facts and the right to control matter. Review each role with evidence, and keep the result separate from federal tax and wage-law classifications.

keyTerms.meaning: Texas Workforce Commission, the agency giving the cited unemployment-tax guidance.
An information-reporting form for the Internal Revenue Service, the U.S. federal tax agency; issuing it does not determine worker status under this Texas test.
The power to direct relevant work, which can matter even when the company does not exercise it.
The specific state tax context of this inquiry, rather than a single classification answer for all employment laws.

The miscellaneous poster contains its own extra-pay and credit notes and says no tip credit is available. Do not import a restaurant hospitality credit into another wage order. sections.heading: An owner-hours claim needs more than a manager job title

It alleges they lacked evidence that those new operators could profitably run the proposed studios on that basis. The complaint also describes owners reporting more work than expected. These remain allegations.

For your own expansion, separate the manager’s paid duties from the owner’s remaining work at launch and during established trading. Include teaching, customer acquisition, absence cover and difficult decisions. Hiring a manager does not demonstrate that the owner’s skills have been replaced at the assumed cost.

It alleges differences in experience, size, contract obligations, curriculum freedom and fees, selective data inclusion and some combined multi-studio results presented as a single studio.

Paragraph 118 reports a 2022 FDD comparison: $75,950 stated average 2021 EBITDA for the combined studio group versus $17,584 for New Franchisee studios. These are historical figures reported in the complaint, not this site’s verified unit accounts or a forecast for your brand.

Current FDD Item 19 addresses financial performance representations: claims about financial results such as sales or earnings. It contains required disclosure even if the brand does not elect to make such a claim. When a claim is made, a reasonable basis, written supporting evidence, relevant historical group details or forecast assumptions and required qualifications matter. Ask what outlets and costs the figures describe before assuming an average represents the model being offered.

Every historical comparison here is attributed to the complaint. The fictional brand in the later exercise should record comparable outlets and actual owner tasks, not reuse these figures or assume that hiring a manager reproduces an expert owner-operator’s result.

title: Who is responsible when a broker recruits franchisees?
description: Keep the broker’s sales conduct and the franchisor’s disclosure duties visible in the same recruitment process.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A broker agreement does not transfer every legal duty
paragraphs: The federal definition of franchise seller is broad: it can include the brand’s people and outside brokers involved in selling. The rule restricts specified seller conduct, while responsibility for furnishing the FDD rests with the franchisor. Those are related but different responsibilities.

The brand therefore needs more than a referral contract stating that the broker “handles compliance.” Identify who speaks to prospects, whose offering is sold, who approves materials and who controls formal disclosure. The actual sales activity matters, including introductions that contain substantive claims.

sections.heading: Control spoken and private messages too
paragraphs: Review presentations, webinars, broker portals, private messages and conversations about likely sales or profit. Sellers must not contradict required disclosures or misrepresent a reference as independent. Performance claims need the applicable reasonable basis, written supporting evidence and disclosure treatment.

A broker’s personal spreadsheet or informal answer can create the same review question as a polished recruitment slide. Give sellers approved materials and a named contact for questions they cannot answer from them. Preserve the version actually used, not just the current master file.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the predictable-margin introduction
paragraphs: A broker introduces a cleaning brand to a “territory investor” and says an employed local manager can produce a predictable margin. The expansion lead does not assume that calling it an introduction removes the sales claim.

The team preserves the exact statement, pauses its reuse and compares it with the relevant Item 19 treatment and supporting material. It also checks which FDD was supplied and by whom. The issue is not solved by renaming the candidate an investor. This example identifies a review task; it does not find that a particular transaction violated the rule.

The filled record separates the broker’s statement from the franchisor’s document-delivery job. Giving one employee both tasks can be an internal arrangement; it does not turn a referral contract into a transfer of every legal duty. The claims-review assignment is an optional internal business role, not a newly prescribed legal office.

Formal disclosure
The broker introduction does not establish which FDD the prospect received.
The franchisor’s disclosure owner checks the document, recipient and timetable separately.

sections.heading: Make a seller-responsibility sheet
paragraphs: Use the sheet as a business control supporting the actual duties. It is not a state authorisation to sell.
bullets: Name every speaker, contracting entity, channel, payment arrangement and permitted territory.
Identify who approves materials and who answers earnings questions.
Assign current-FDD delivery, receipt records and timetable checks to named people.
Keep the actual communications and document versions with the prospect’s file.
Check separate state broker, advertising, registration and sales requirements before relying on the process.

practicalOutput: A named seller-responsibility sheet linking approved claims, current documents, prospect records and formal disclosure duties.
limitations: This is the federal seller/conduct distinction. State broker licensing, registration, advertising and sales authorisation require independent review.
learningSummary: A broker can introduce candidates and help sell a franchise, but hiring one does not make the brand’s disclosure responsibilities disappear. The federal rule reaches several people involved in franchise sales. Decide who may say what, who supplies the FDD and who checks the timetable before recruitment begins.

keyTerms.meaning: The business granting franchise rights and responsible for furnishing the FDD.
The independent business buying and operating under those rights.
The broad federal category including relevant employees, agents, subfranchisors and third-party brokers involved in sales.
The FDD section addressing financial performance representations, such as specified sales or profit claims.

title: How should you check a franchise recruitment advertisement?
description: Read the claim as a prospect sees it, then connect it to the disclosure and supporting evidence.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Compare the actual advertisement with the disclosure
paragraphs: Franchise sellers must not make claims that contradict required disclosures. Financial performance representations must also satisfy the applicable basis, written-support and disclosure conditions. Not every brand message is a performance representation; assess what this message communicates.

An earnings or sales figure should be checked against Item 19 and the actual supporting material. A promising result from the home market does not alone justify the U.S. claim. A disclaimer or broker label does not cure a contradiction with required disclosure.

sections.heading: Keep the context with the number
paragraphs: Save the image, caption, landing page and spoken presentation together. Distinguish revenue from profit, identify included and excluded units, and record geography, period and operating model. Those facts help explain what a number does and does not show.

Review testimonials and any incentive given to a reference, including a claim that the reference is independent. When source information changes, find every live advertisement using it rather than correcting one slide while an older version remains on a broker portal.

sections.heading: Fictional example: turning a past margin into a target
paragraphs: A technical-services brand has one home-country unit with a 20% operating margin. Its U.S. recruitment deck says “target 20%.” Finance initially regards the word target as enough explanation.

The review instead asks what a prospective partner would understand, whether there is a reasonable basis for the U.S. statement, which costs and units the result includes, and how the claim is disclosed. Calling an achieved figure a target does not answer those questions. The team pauses or revises the slide according to the review rather than treating this fictional number as an approved forecast.

The useful decision is not simply whether 20% is arithmetically correct. It is whether this complete message, for this audience, has the necessary basis and treatment. An optional internal claim register can record revise or pause while the missing facts are resolved; it does not itself approve the advertisement.

The word target does not supply a reasonable basis, written support or the required disclosure treatment.

An accurate percentage can still leave the prospect with an unsupported impression.

The slide may also appear on a landing page or broker portal.
Changing the master slide does not establish that every old version was withdrawn.

sections.heading: Record a decision for each usable version
paragraphs: The claim register is an optional management tool supporting the legal requirements. Record approve, revise or pause, the responsible person and the remaining evidence needed.
bullets: Write each quantitative or implied performance statement exactly.
Link it to the corresponding disclosure and written support.
Keep context, exclusions, period and sample information visible.
Track every approved channel and withdraw superseded versions.
Check state advertising filings, required wording and sales requirements separately before publication.

limitations: No particular advertisement is approved here. State advertising filing/legend rules, broker rules and sales authority remain separate.
learningSummary: A recruitment campaign can create expectations about revenue, profit and support before a prospect reads the FDD. The wording, image and surrounding explanation all matter. Review the actual message rather than assuming a disclaimer or the word “target” makes a performance claim acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: The Franchise Disclosure Document describing the offering for prospective franchisees.
A statement about specified actual or potential financial results, requiring the applicable legal treatment.
Written evidence supporting a claim, including the relevant data and limitations.
An internal list of proposed statements, their support, approved wording and live versions.
