sections.heading: Fictional example: two territories and national accounts
paragraphs: A Belgian industrial-services brand promises two operators exclusive service territories while retaining national accounts. The operations director draws the geography and records which customers, leads and account types each promise includes. If both operators are told they have exclusive rights to the same customers, the problem cannot be resolved by a map that was never explained in the sales materials.

The director therefore checks the presentations, contract wording and support promises together under the applicable business-opportunity rules. If one operator later misses targets, that is a new decision: the team separately examines section 407.400 coverage, proposed exit, notice and any exception. An accurate original territory statement does not by itself permit immediate termination.

sections.heading: Use the remedy provision for the actual claim
paragraphs: Section 407.410 contains different remedies in different subsections. Subsection 1’s double-consideration and attorney-fee wording concerns inducing participation in a pyramid sales scheme. It must not be imported into an ordinary franchise notice dispute simply because it appears nearby.

Subsection 2 separately permits a franchisee damaged by failure to give required cancellation or termination notice to seek the listed damages, including loss of goodwill, costs and appropriate equitable relief. Keep evidence of coverage, the required notice and failure, causation and actual loss. The provision does not predict an award, and the complete judicial application was not researched here.

sections.heading: Keep a sales file and an exit file
paragraphs: The two files can share the agreement while answering different questions. A sales file records what the buyer was promised. An exit file records why the relationship is being changed and how the applicable notice rule is being addressed.

sections.heading: Assign the next concrete review
paragraphs: Before an offer, have the responsible person compare the territory allocation and promises against the written agreement. Before an exit, have that person identify the relationship coverage and exact notice or exception branch. Neither exercise establishes a universal state FDD period or the absence of a registration requirement.
Preserve unresolved questions in the record instead of treating one narrow conclusion as permission for every part of the transaction. Federal franchise disclosure remains an independent question.

It establishes neither a universal state disclosure period nor absence of registration. Federal, sector-dealer, competition, employment, tax and local requirements need independent review.
learningSummary: A brand can face one question when promising a territory and another when ending an operator’s rights. Missouri’s business-opportunity rules address specified sales promises, while its franchise relationship rules have their own coverage and notice requirements. Keep both decisions clear in the commercial documents and management record.

title: Montana construction-equipment dealers: exit rules and separate stock repurchase
description: Construction-equipment dealer protections and inventory repurchase rules require separate coverage and evidence checks.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Adding equipment can change the legal questions
paragraphs: Montana’s construction-equipment dealership provisions in part 9 have their own definitions. MCA 30-11-901 includes oral, written, express and implied arrangements and a community of interest in distributing construction equipment. A written service agreement may therefore not be the only relevant evidence.

List the actual equipment, sales and service rights, supplier relationships and communications. Separate retail equipment, wholesale distribution and branded services. This part is not a general definition of a business-format franchise; the equipment and arrangement must fit the particular scope.

sections.heading: Good cause is different from a notice period
paragraphs: Under MCA 30-11-902, a grantor needs good cause for a covered termination, cancellation, nonrenewal or substantial competitive change, and bears the burden of proving it. A substantial competitive change concerns the covered dealer’s competitive circumstances; identify the actual proposed conduct rather than relying on a vague label.

A contract clause or missed sales target does not by itself prove statutory good cause. Retain the requirements, performance facts, treatment of comparable dealers and relevant communications. Even where cause is established, the applicable notice and correction provisions remain a separate question.

sections.heading: Choose the actual notice branch
paragraphs: MCA 30-11-903 generally requires 90 days’ prior notice by certified mail and 60 days to rectify claimed deficiencies. Preserve the notice method, reasons and correction evidence rather than substituting an ordinary email for the specified mailing process.

Nonpayment has a separate 10-day notice and remedy rule. Stated insolvency, assignment-for-creditors and bankruptcy grounds have different notice treatment under subsections (2) and (3). An assignment for creditors is an arrangement concerning assets for the benefit of creditors. Do not apply the ordinary 90/60 timing universally or assume an alleged financial problem satisfies a listed exception.

The operations director first records the equipment, distribution rights and actual relationship to test part 9 coverage. If covered, the supplier needs to address good cause and its proof burden, then select the correct notice and correction branch. The missed target is evidence to assess, not automatic permission for immediate exit. A separate inventory review then asks which stock, if any, qualifies for repurchase.

sections.heading: Value stock under the repurchase rules, not the whole spreadsheet
paragraphs: Part 7 contains a distinct inventory repurchase regime with its own definitions, including industrial and construction equipment and repair parts. Do not assume part 9 coverage automatically decides every part 7 issue.

Review the qualifying contract, inventory condition, price basis and exclusions. Finance should retain stock age, invoices, freight, title and condition records. A spare part appearing on an inventory spreadsheet is not proof that its full listed value is recoverable.

title: Nebraska recruitment: qualifying franchise notice versus SAMP filing
description: Understand the difference between a qualifying franchise notice and the separate seller-assisted marketing-plan process.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Why the campaign needs a legal decision first
paragraphs: A brand may prepare a website, book a Nebraska recruitment advertisement and arrange calls with prospective operators before anyone signs a contract. Nebraska’s relevant filing trigger can arise during that earlier activity. The selling business therefore needs a decision before the campaign, not only a check on signing day.

Section 59-1722 creates a conditional franchise exemption from the SAMP Act. The current statute incorporates specified federal provisions as they existed on January 1, 2026. Establishing the exemption means checking those incorporated conditions; using the word licence or holding a completed FDD does not establish compliance by itself.

sections.heading: What the qualifying franchise route requires
paragraphs: The statute requires notice and a $100 fee before the specified Nebraska-based advertising, offers or representations to Nebraska prospects. Some state prohibitions remain applicable despite the exemption. Describe where the advertisement is placed, who receives the offer and which entity is selling, so the reviewer can apply the actual trigger.

The notice identifies the seller, contact details, operating name and plan description. The regulator describes the qualifying franchise notice as a one-time filing without renewal, while distinguishing contact-only amendments from other changes. Keep that distinction when updating the company record: “one time” is not a reason to ignore every later change. Acknowledgment records a filing event; it does not approve the offering or verify statements about profit.

sections.heading: If the exemption is not established, investigate the other route
paragraphs: A covered nonexempt SAMP has a different process. Section 59-1724 provides for a prior disclosure filing and $100 fee, material-change filings and annual updates. A material change is a change important to the required information; it cannot simply be parked until the next sales cycle.

Section 59-1732 also addresses disclosure at the first specified in-person or written communication and at least 48 hours before the relevant contract or consideration. Those state rules do not shorten an independently applicable federal disclosure period. First determine which rules cover the transaction, then put each applicable clock on the calendar.

sections.heading: Choose one route for the training campaign before scheduling it
paragraphs: The UK network’s advertisement, first communication and planned deposit are separate inputs. Establish the actual route before using its timetable.

Its manager has a draft FDD and assumes the next step is accepting deposits. Instead, the manager lists the advertisement date, intended recipients, first communications and proposed commitments.

The reviewer establishes whether the actual offer satisfies the conditional franchise exemption. If it does, the company arranges the required prior notice and fee and keeps the acknowledgment. If it does not, the manager pauses the assumed franchise-notice route and obtains a decision on the nonexempt SAMP requirements. This planning sequence prevents the wrong form from becoming the basis for the campaign.

The seller must first establish which legal route applies to its actual offer. Preparing disclosure documents and obtaining a state filing acknowledgment are separate tasks, and neither proves that sales claims are accurate.

title: Nevada farm-equipment dealers: plan changes and exit before signing
description: Understand why equipment inventory and dependence on a supplier can create duties beyond the brand agreement.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Why this is an equipment question
paragraphs: Nevada NRS 597.112–597.118 concerns defined farm-equipment dealer relationships. Its tests include retail inventory rights, a distribution-system role and substantial dependence on a supplier. Inventory means the defined farm equipment, attachments or repair parts. A maintenance-service brand or software licence does not fit merely because the parties use the word dealer.

The supplier and proposed operator should list the actual machines, parts, distribution rights and sources of revenue. That list helps the reviewer apply the statutory definition instead of copying a rule from another industry.

sections.heading: Termination and nonrenewal have a particular procedure
paragraphs: Section 597.1143 addresses good cause and generally requires 180 days’ written reasons before termination or nonrenewal, with 60 days to correct specified deficiencies. Listed grounds receive different treatment, and market-share failures have an assistance condition. The general periods therefore cannot be applied without checking the reason for action.

A contractual end date does not complete the analysis. Keep the alleged deficiency, performance evidence, support offered and proposed corrective steps together. They help explain whether the applicable statutory branch has been followed; simply waiting out a notice period cannot establish good cause.

sections.heading: A major amendment is not automatically governed by the same clock
paragraphs: Section 597.1143(1) also requires good cause for a substantial change of a covered agreement’s terms. Section 597.115(4) addresses termination, nonrenewal and those changes because of natural disaster, labour dispute or similar circumstances beyond the dealer’s control. Section 597.118 prohibits waiver or modification of the statutory rights, obligations and liabilities.

The 180-day notice and 60-day correction provisions in subsections (2)–(3) concern termination and nonrenewal. They do not establish a universal 180-day notice for every amendment. Compare the old and proposed terms and explain why the supplier wants the change.

sections.heading: Choose the farm-machine action before copying a notice
paragraphs: These comparisons apply only after the defined farm-equipment relationship is established.

Later, the manufacturer considers changing the agreement substantially or ending it after weak sales. The manager first checks whether the arrangement falls within the farm-equipment definitions.

The team then separates the proposed action from its reason. A substantial amendment raises the good-cause question; a termination or nonrenewal also requires the correct notice and correction analysis. If the problem is market share, the assistance condition needs attention. If a natural disaster affected performance, the separate uncontrollable-circumstances provision must be examined. The same notice template cannot answer every branch.

sections.heading: Keep the possible buyback separate from the accounting balance
paragraphs: The chapter has repurchase rules and exclusions based on inventory condition, age and other facts, including specified supplier-required systems and tools. Retain purchase and requirement records now. Neither the gross inventory total nor the amount spent on technology proves what must be bought back.

Assign separate reviews for franchise sales and other industry or local duties.

Coverage, good cause, notice exceptions and repurchase eligibility require actual facts; federal disclosure and other state, sector and local duties are separate.
learningSummary: A company selling farm machines through a Nevada dealer may have to plan for more than the contract’s end date. The defined farm-equipment dealer law addresses reasons for major changes, termination, notice and inventory repurchase. Establish whether that law covers the arrangement before applying any of its numbers.

title: New Hampshire chain-distributor review: participant payments and recruiting rights
description: Learn how to examine successive recruitment rights without assuming a master-operator title decides the legal result.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the actual offer, not its name
paragraphs: A supplier might call its partner a master franchisee, regional licensee or representative. Those words can describe business responsibilities, but they do not establish whether the sales arrangement meets RSA 358-B. The reviewed law focuses on a particular combination of required investment and successive recruiting rights.

The test concerns participants who make an investment and receive rights to recruit others for economic gain, with those further participants also investing and receiving recruiting rights. Read the complete arrangement through each level. A recruitment fee alone, or genuine master-operator duties alone, does not establish every element.

sections.heading: Why a territory limit does not answer the question
paragraphs: The law expressly says that limiting the number of participants or adding eligibility conditions does not itself change the identity of the defined scheme. A cap can affect the commercial scale without resolving the statutory structure.

Where the prohibited device is established, the chapter prohibits promotion, offering or granting participation. The company therefore needs the review before recruitment activity, rather than waiting to see whether the network becomes large or profitable. This page does not conclude that every multi-level business or master franchise is unlawful.

sections.heading: Separate customers from participants in the accounts
paragraphs: A useful management exercise is to draw two money flows: revenue from delivering services to customers, and payments connected with joining or recruiting into the network. Identify each recipient and the conditions for earning each amount. This is a planning method for exposing the facts, not an independent legal safe harbour.

Also describe the support actually delivered. Training, site visits and quality checks have costs and responsible people. An unsupported statement that a payment buys “support” does not show what the parties do. Conversely, documenting real support does not replace applying the complete statutory test.

sections.heading: Follow the technical network’s payment through the levels
paragraphs: Keep customer-service revenue separate from joining/recruitment money. The table does not declare every master arrangement prohibited.

The expansion manager instead draws the arrangement across several levels. For each participant, the manager records required payments, recruiting rights and the source of compensation. A separate column records customer service revenue and actual training or field-support duties. The board can now ask whether the economic arrangement meets every element of the defined chain-distributor device, rather than treating the territory cap as an exemption.

If the review identifies unresolved facts, the next step is to clarify the contracts and payment plan before promoting participation. The fictional example demonstrates the investigation; it does not determine whether any particular arrangement is prohibited.

To understand the distinction, trace what each participant must pay, what recruiting rights they receive and how money moves through the network.

Its place-of-business wording includes qualifying offices or warehouses from which personnel visit or call customers, or goods are delivered.

That wording makes the real operation worth investigating. It does not mean every warehouse qualifies. Record what happens at the location, what is sold, how customers are contacted and whether most sales are directly to consumers or business buyers. A cited 2025 federal district-court opinion explains why calling an arrangement distribution does not resolve those factual questions. The federally registered-mark exception is located within the marketing-programme limb of section 66-94(4). It does not erase the other listed representations. A registration in the home country or a pending U.S. application is not a substitute for the stated U.S. registration condition.

Section 66-94.1 provides a separate responsible-seller exemption with its own conditions and sworn filing. A sworn filing is a formal statement made with the required verification. A company’s good reputation alone does not establish this exemption.

Section 1334.12 contains other exceptions. In cases under sections 1334.08 or 1334.09, section 1334.14 places proof of an exemption or exception on the person claiming it. A written explanation linked to the facts is therefore more useful than an unexplained box marked exempt.

title: Pennsylvania vehicle-dealer inventory buyback: return and payment events

sections.heading: Check the business and the property first
paragraphs: The Board of Vehicles Act has defined vehicle-dealer and franchise coverage. Section 316 concerns eligible inventory and equipment after specified termination or nonrenewal events. A cleaning or IT brand cannot use these numbers as a general service-franchise exit formula.

Even for a relevant dealer, the accounting category “stock” is too broad to decide eligibility. Product category, condition, acquisition age and other statutory limits matter. Motorcycle, recreational-vehicle and manufactured-housing arrangements need particular attention to their treatment under the section.

sections.heading: There are two events and two clocks
paragraphs: Section 316 generally requires covered property to be returned within 90 days of the relevant termination or nonrenewal. It separately requires repurchase/payment within 60 days of tender. The starting events differ: a relationship’s effective end date is not automatically the date property was tendered.

The company should obtain return instructions and retain the evidence of tender and actual return. Neither an invoice total nor an assumption that the 90 days have passed establishes when the payment clock began. Apply the precise statutory event and eligibility requirements before calculating any claimed due date.

The team separates each category. Vehicle rows show serial numbers, acquisition dates, mileage and condition. Parts rows include the relevant catalogue records. Tools and signs have their own purchase and requirement evidence. Any secured creditor is identified rather than being overlooked in a general stock total.

The operations manager then links the inventory file to the effective termination/nonrenewal event and to the return instructions, tender evidence and return record. paragraphs: Keeping these records from the start is a business planning choice that makes a later review possible. It does not enlarge the statutory categories. A dealer may have spent money that is commercially important but does not fall within the relevant repurchase provision.

The same distinction matters when pricing a new relationship. Budgeting for inventory, tools and financing is sensible, but management should not assume that every amount is recoverable at exit. Use the actual statutory category and conditions rather than describing section 316 as an automatic refund of the investment.

sections.heading: A mark is one fact, not the complete answer

Assistance placing vending machines or similar devices, purchases of products made by the buyer, and guarantee/refund promises have their own terms.

Keep the filing receipt and assigned number with the campaign record. A registration number identifies the relevant filing; it is not a government endorsement of the business. Statements about state compliance have separate limits.

paragraphs: For the cleaning-brand example, the useful question is which promise creates which task. A single brand-registration answer cannot replace this comparison.

title: Utah franchise notices: obtain the receipt before the covered offer

sections.heading: The trigger includes offers to a Utah resident
paragraphs: Section 13-15-201(2) requires proof of notice receipt before a person offers or sells a franchise to be located in Utah or to a Utah resident. The team must therefore investigate both the proposed operation and the person receiving the offer.

sections.heading: Use the section effective May 6, 2026
paragraphs: The reviewed current section, amended effective May 6, 2026, makes the receipt valid for one year from issue. Renewal compliance is due at least 30 days before expiry. Filing information that becomes incorrect or incomplete must be updated within 30 days.

These are different dates. Keep the issue date and expiry with the receipt, then record the date information becomes incorrect or incomplete. An annual renewal reminder may arrive too late to catch a change that requires an earlier update.

sections.heading: Build the calendar from four different events

paragraphs: Fictional example: a UK technical-services brand plans a campaign directed to a Utah-resident prospect. The sales owner separately records formal FDD delivery and the earliest proposed commitment. This prevents one receipt from being used as evidence of several unrelated events. paragraphs: The Act distinguishes the qualifying franchise notice from the general business-opportunity disclosure filing. Section 201(2)(c) directs those who do not qualify for the notice route to subsection (1), which has its own content and ten-business-day purchaser-disclosure provisions.

title: Vermont equipment partners: choose the right exit process before using a deadline

sections.heading: Determine what the operator sells
paragraphs: Vermont Title 9, Chapter 107 concerns defined equipment and machinery dealerships. The dealer and inventory definitions matter even though the agreement may be oral or written. Heavy construction equipment and a specified single-line dealer category are excluded.

A pure service franchise is not established as covered merely because it uses a trademark. Describe the actual machines, parts, repair work and branded services. Separate activities in the factual file so the reviewer can apply the definitions and exclusions to what the parties really do.

paragraphs: Section 4072 generally requires cause, 120 days’ notice and a 60-day opportunity to correct the stated problem. It has a separate market-penetration termination process involving an initial 24-month period and a final notice period. Specified events permit immediate termination.

The reason for ending the agreement therefore affects the route to examine. A supplier should retain the actual performance requirements, notice history and reasons, rather than treating 120 days as a universal instruction or assuming an immediate-termination exception applies.

sections.heading: Choose a reason-to-process branch before using a deadline
paragraphs: For the Dutch service-plus-equipment example, classify the equipment relationship first, then the intended exit event, then the requested inventory. Those are three separate decisions.

paragraphs: Fictional example: a Dutch industrial-services brand adds utility-equipment sales and repairs to its Vermont partner offer. Its original service budget did not account for a warehouse of supplier inventory or the consequences of ending an equipment relationship.

The operations manager separates the equipment, repair and service rights and checks whether the defined dealer relationship is present. If a later performance problem arises, the manager records the requirement, evidence and event being considered. A market-penetration issue is not automatically assigned the same procedure as another termination ground.

Finance maintains item records from purchase: age, source, condition and title. If repurchase is later requested, those records allow a review of eligible items and values. The team does not assume that every line in the inventory account will be reimbursed or that every exit uses the same clock. This fictional exercise does not decide coverage or cause.

sections.heading: A buyback claim needs more than a stock total
paragraphs: Sections 4073–4074 address repurchase subject to request, eligibility, valuation and payment requirements. Record what is requested, by whom and when, and link it to the particular items and applicable conditions.

Keeping an inventory ledger and planning possible cash exposure are management methods. They do not establish a legal entitlement or enlarge the items covered. The payment owner should budget an obligation only after identifying the actual statutory branch and evidence.

Assign valuation, return and payment questions, alongside separate franchise/operating-law review.

title: West Virginia equipment dealers: map inventory, repairs and the exit process
description: Learn why the dealer definition and item records matter before applying the six-month termination rule or estimating repurchase.

sections.heading: The title does not limit the inquiry to farm machines
paragraphs: The Farm Equipment Dealer Contract Act includes specified retail sellers of construction, industrial and outdoor power equipment, with inventory and repair-service conditions. Those conditions are part of coverage, not optional background facts.

The supplier and operator should record what is sold at retail, which inventory obligations exist and who provides repairs. A brand licence or service contract alone does not establish that the Act applies. Conversely, a business should not ignore the Act simply because its equipment is industrial rather than agricultural.

sections.heading: Notice is a procedure, not only a period
paragraphs: Section 47-11F-3 generally requires six months’ termination notice, prescribed written service and stated contents. Listed exceptions and a mutual-consent route need separate examination. Keep the reason, method, contents and effective date together.

Do not casually replace six months with an assumed number of days or treat an informal message as proof of prescribed service. Nor does the existence of a contract clause settle whether the relevant statutory branch and exception have been followed. This guide does not choose a termination route for any actual relationship.

Section 47-11F-3: how would termination be notified?
The general rule is six months’ notice, with prescribed written service and contents. Listed exceptions and a mutual-consent route need separate review.

If the supplier later proposes termination, the secretary identifies the actual event and examines the notice method, contents, date and any claimed exception or mutual-consent route. sections.heading: Inventory value and payment are different questions

sections.heading: First identify the buyer and transaction
paragraphs: D.C. section 28-3901 includes franchises and business opportunities in its goods-and-services definition. The same chapter separately defines consumer, merchant and transaction concepts. A merchant is the relevant supplier under the law; the fact that a franchise is mentioned does not automatically decide every business-to-business purchase or dispute.

Section 28-3904 addresses covered material misstatements and omissions. Describe the actual buyer, purpose, seller and transaction before applying that rule. Keep current application notes with the source review rather than assuming that every printed change has the same implemented effect.

sections.heading: Write down what “all permissions included” actually means
paragraphs: A sales presentation may mix promises about training, brand use, company registration, taxes and premises permissions. Separate those statements. For each claimed approval or licence, identify the issuing body, the holder, the activity, the location and what remains to be done.

This is useful even before the legal coverage question is resolved: it lets the management team see whether its statement matches the documents. It does not establish permission to sell or substitute for required formal disclosure.

sections.heading: The operating process has several different steps
paragraphs: The Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, known as DLCP, separates corporate and trade-name registration from tax registration, zoning or home-occupation/occupancy requirements, and the activity-based Basic Business License application. One completed step should not be treated as proof that all the others are complete.

For example, registering a company establishes a different fact from whether its chosen premises may be used for the proposed activity. Keep a shared list of the companies and addresses, but retain separate confirmations for each process. None of these records alone proves compliance with franchise sales law or a Franchise Disclosure Document requirement. An FDD is the prescribed information for a prospective franchise buyer, not an operating permit.

sections.heading: Test the training network’s all-permissions promise
paragraphs: A promise-to-document comparison is useful before the coverage decision, but is not permission to sell or open.

headers: Why it is not the whole answer
rows: A company or trade-name record exists
Its actual holder and legal/business name.
It does not determine the activity’s zoning, occupancy or licence.
The brand has an operating permission
Issuing body, holder, activity and address.
A brand-held record does not establish the operator’s own required permission.
The operator has a Basic Business License
The actual activity-based licence and holder.
It does not establish franchise disclosure compliance or validate the sales pitch.
The pitch says all permissions are included
The actual statement and any omitted unfinished steps.
CPPA coverage still requires the consumer, merchant and transaction analysis.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a training network enters D.C.
paragraphs: A European training brand tells a prospective local operator that all local permissions are included. Its operations director asks for the actual records. Some may belong to the brand, while a tax account, premises permission or activity licence may depend on the operator and its address.

The director makes a list showing the holder and unfinished step for each permission. The reviewer also examines whether the buyer and transaction fall within the CPPA’s definitions. The answer cannot be inferred from the word franchise or from the existence of a Basic Business License. If the broad sales promise is unsupported, it needs review against what the business can actually document.

sections.heading: Prepare two practical lists
bullets: Keep a claims list containing the actual licensing, approval, support and financial statements used in the pitch.
Keep an operating-permissions list naming the company, trade name, address, activity, issuing authority and responsible person.
Identify who provides support and who must obtain each permission.
Record the consumer, merchant and transaction facts and the relevant application notes.
Leave federal disclosure and unresolved D.C. franchise-sales questions as explicit tasks.

practicalOutput: A sales-claims checklist supported by actual records, plus a separate company-and-premises permissions list with named owners.
limitations: The CPPA reference does not establish that every B2B operator is a consumer or that every franchise sale has the same result.
This guide does not complete D.C. franchise, dealer, employment, tax, industry or local opening requirements, and it does not authorize an offer, opening or termination.
learningSummary: A prospective operator may be told that a business package includes all the permissions needed to open. Before making that promise, the seller should identify which permissions actually exist and which depend on the buyer, activity or premises. A local business licence does not also prove that franchise-sales and disclosure requirements have been met.

keyTerms.meaning: The D.C. consumer-protection law discussed here; its own consumer, merchant and transaction definitions matter.
A statement, or missing fact, important enough to affect the relevant decision; the cited provisions address misleading conduct within their coverage.
